note: Line-focused concentrators: parabolic trough (PTC) and linear Fresnel / compact linear Fresnel reflectors (LFR/CLFR), single-axis tracking, for medium (75-150 degC) and high (150-400 degC) temperature rises.

Line-focused collectors heat the working fluid to about half of point-focus levels, with the possibility of reaching 550 degC (CSP context); SHIP use is limited to about 400 degC (p.3). reprinted from refs [23-26]
Lower bound of the medium temperature-rise class, the lowest class ticked for PTC and LFR; class boundary, not a measured limit.
Point-focused concentrators: solar power tower (heliostat field) and parabolic dish, two-axis tracking; the tower is relevant for temperature rises above 150 degC.
Tower and dish can heat the working fluid in the absorber to above 1000 degC (CSP context). reprinted from refs [17-22]
Stationary non-concentrating collectors (flat plate unevacuated/evacuated, evacuated tube, unglazed, air, PVT); concentration is not justified below 75 degC.

Table 2 ticks the high temperature-rise class (150-400 degC) for flat-plate (unevacuated and evacuated) and evacuated-tube collectors; air, PVT and unglazed collectors only below 75 degC. Class boundary from a classification table - weak.
